title: Ragdoll Reality Weapons List & Weapon Types
description: Explore Ragdoll Reality weapons by type, from Grab and Bat to Shotgun, C4, and more. See the confirmed weapon names and where to find unlock help.

hero.heading: Ragdoll Reality Weapons List
hero.lead: Ragdoll Reality advertises 20+ weapons and interactions. This directory identifies the twelve names in its official Roblox description, groups them for quick reference, and separates confirmed names from unknown unlock requirements.

sections.heading: Ragdoll Reality Weapons at a Glance
sections.intro: The official game description names twelve options and says the total selection exceeds twenty. These names are verified from the public listing; the complete current in-game menu, individual stats, and unlock thresholds are not included in that listing.

subsections.heading: What Counts as a Listed Weapon?
paragraphs: Fists, Push, and Grab appear alongside the firearms and tools in the game's advertised weapon line. For that reason, this directory calls them 'named equipment and actions' rather than pretending all twelve are ordinary buyable gun items.

An item that is named by the developer is not necessarily unlocked at the beginning of every session. We distinguish knowing the name from knowing how to access it. Use the separate unlock page for the progress mechanism.

sections.heading: All Ragdoll Reality Weapons Confirmed by the Game Page
sections.intro: Group names by what a player is looking for in the equipment list. These are plain-language navigation categories; they do not claim to reflect an official rarity system or upgrade tree.

subsections.heading: Hand and Melee Actions
paragraphs: Fists provide an unarmed option; Push describes moving another body without firing a projectile; Grab is the named handling interaction for carrying, throwing, or manipulating a dummy. The Bat and Machete are the two explicitly named close-range tools in the listing.

These five options are best understood by their interaction type. The official description does not provide melee reach, damage, attack speed, or a starting equipment allowance. Try them in the game and compare what you actually see rather than assuming a 'free starter' designation.

subsections.heading: Guns and Ranged Weapons
paragraphs: Pistol, Shotgun, Sniper, and Minigun are the four clearly named conventional firearms. Rocket Launcher is a listed projectile or launcher option but is placed separately in the reference table because an explosive launcher is not directly comparable to a handgun.

A firearm category does not establish precise ammunition capacity or reload behavior. The public listing describes hit-location reactions but does not publish damage multipliers or weapon firing data. A precise ranking would require controlled gameplay trials.

subsections.heading: Fire and Explosive Options
paragraphs: Flamethrower and C4 are explicitly named by the developer. Their ordinary English names suggest fire and explosive interactions, respectively, but their exact in-game duration, detonation method, and access conditions require confirmation inside a session.

Do not assume C4 is unlocked at a particular kill count, that Flamethrower has a specific fuel limit, or that an explosive weapon is always strongest. Choose based on the mechanic you want to try, then observe the live game result.

sections.heading: How to Use This Ragdoll Reality Weapon Directory
sections.intro: The list is designed to answer a lookup question before the player needs a separate unlock tutorial. Start with the name, identify its broad class, and then verify the availability state in the version you are playing.

subsections.heading: Names Are Confirmed; Individual Requirements Are Not
paragraphs: The official Roblox page confirms the roster is larger than twelve, but names only twelve entries. A claimed complete list of twenty-plus individually named items would need independent current-game evidence. We therefore avoid silently filling in the unnamed slots with guesses.

The same applies to conditions: there is an overall kills-to-unlock mechanic, yet no reliable public table of 'weapon X costs Y kills'. The table deliberately says 'Not stated publicly' rather than using zero or a fake requirement.

subsections.heading: Check the Weapon Interface in Your Current Session
paragraphs: Open the real experience from Roblox, look at the weapons or equipment options displayed in your current build, and compare the names against the directory. If an item is unavailable, note any requirement shown on screen. Exact menu labels can differ across platforms and updates.

A useful personal record is the weapon name, whether it appears locked, the wording of any condition visible in-game, and the date checked. This helps distinguish a new unlock from an outdated guide description.

sections.heading: Which Weapons Should Beginners Try First?
sections.intro: Without official stats or repeatable tests, it is more useful to choose an interaction by purpose than to publish an invented S-to-D tier list.

subsections.heading: Choose by Interaction, Not a Fake Power Ranking
paragraphs: To learn how body-location physics react, start with whatever basic action your account currently has accessible. To inspect a ranged reaction, choose an accessible named gun. If you want a broader environmental reaction, try a named launcher or explosive only when the game permits it.

Comparisons should involve the same scene, the same target state, and an actual observation. Visual impact does not provide a numeric damage value; do not confuse an interesting animation with verified weapon superiority.

subsections.heading: Use the Playground as a Test Environment
paragraphs: The official page lists the 80-stud tower, shredder, train, spike pit, wrecking ball, human cannon, and seesaw. These map features are useful contexts for physics experiments, although each has its own layout and timing. A weapon name alone does not tell you how it interacts with every hazard.

For a cleaner observation, change one condition at a time. Test a single item, watch the dummy's response, then switch to another. That is an experiment a player can perform without requiring any unsupported numerical 'best weapon' label.

sections.heading: How Weapon Unlocks and Updates Affect This List
sections.intro: The developer states that new weapons can unlock through kills and that the experience receives weekly updates. Because the game is changing, screenshots and old purchase claims should be checked against the live build.

subsections.heading: Unlock Progress Is a Different Question
paragraphs: If you already know a weapon's name but cannot access it, read the specific unlock guide. That page explains how to check kill-based progression and what the public source does and does not confirm. Duplicating its full tutorial here would make both pages harder to use.
The word 'weapons' belongs to this directory; 'how to unlock' belongs to the procedure page. Keeping those answers separate helps you find the right information quickly.

subsections.heading: How Additions Get Verified
paragraphs: A newly claimed weapon should be added only after its name appears in a dated official description or is independently documented in the live experience. The review date is shown above. Unattributed community guesses or a competitor's URL name are not confirmation of a new piece of equipment.

Source: the official Roblox experience description, which names the twelve entries in this directory. If the developer publishes precise counts, availability or stats, those fields can be added with a new review date.

faq.question: How many weapons are in Ragdoll Reality?
faq.answer: The official description says there are more than twenty. It explicitly names twelve equipment options and actions; this is not a claim that all remaining names are known.

faq.question: What weapons are confirmed in Ragdoll Reality?
faq.answer: Fists, Push, Grab, Pistol, Bat, Machete, Shotgun, Sniper, Minigun, Rocket Launcher, Flamethrower, and C4 are named in the official listing.

faq.question: Is there a verified Ragdoll Reality weapon tier list?
faq.answer: Not from the official description. There are no published damage, range or unlock tables suitable for a numerical ranking.

faq.question: How do I unlock weapons?
faq.answer: The developer says new weapons unlock with kills. Read the dedicated unlock guide and check any exact requirement shown in your current game session.

faq.question: Does each weapon require Robux?
faq.answer: The general official listing does not establish a purchase requirement for each named weapon. Check the in-game availability state and store rather than assuming the same route for all items.

title: How to Unlock Weapons in Ragdoll Reality
description: Learn how weapon unlocks work in Ragdoll Reality, how kills affect progression, and what to check when a weapon remains locked in the current game version.

hero.heading: How to Unlock Weapons in Ragdoll Reality
hero.lead: The official Roblox description states that kills unlock new weapons. Individual kill thresholds and on-screen menu paths are not specified there, so use the game’s current equipment indicators to check your progress.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: What Unlocks New Weapons?
sections.intro: Kills are the developer-confirmed progression method. That is the solid starting point for unlocking a Ragdoll Reality weapon. The listing does not say that every item opens at the same total, or that there is a particular shortcut you must purchase.

subsections.heading: Kills Are the Confirmed Unlock Mechanic
paragraphs: The game description directly links kills to new weapon access. It does not define which dummy or enemy interactions count toward that total, whether consecutive kills matter, or the numerical requirement for each item. Those differences are important when you are trying to troubleshoot a particular lock.

A reasonable approach is to play normally, check a named locked weapon, make a note of its visible requirement if the interface shows one, and inspect that same entry later. That checks what your actual account sees rather than relying on a third-party progression chart.

subsections.heading: What the Description Does Not Tell You
paragraphs: No official per-item threshold list is included in the captured public description. It also does not publish a definitive order of unlocks, any rate multiplier, or a statement that zombie kills count in exactly the same way as other actions.
For this reason, a guide claiming that the Shotgun requires a specific total or that a paid pass halves every requirement would need separate direct evidence. This page does not invent those numbers.

sections.heading: Step-by-Step: Check and Unlock a Weapon
sections.intro: The following workflow uses only the confirmed kills-based mechanic and observations that you can make in the live game; it does not pretend an unverified button layout is universal across PC and mobile.

subsections.heading: Step 1: Open the Official Roblox Experience
paragraphs: Start from the official experience ID 127932298993998. This avoids playing the wrong ragdoll game or following another experience's unrelated currency system. Make sure you are signed into the Roblox account whose equipment you plan to check.
Allow the playable session to load before comparing guidance. Game menus can be rearranged between platform layouts, and screenshots from an older update can differ from the current screen.

subsections.heading: Step 2: Earn Kills and Check Progress
paragraphs: The developer states that kills are used for weapon unlocks. Play and observe the in-game results; if a kill or progression counter is actually visible to you, note its value before and after a comparable action.

Do not assume damage, throwing, infection, and kills are interchangeable. An animation showing a dummy falling is not proof that the game's progression system credited you a kill. The live counter or a changed unlock state is stronger evidence.

subsections.heading: Step 3: Confirm That the Weapon Became Available
paragraphs: Return to the place your current game version displays equipment. Compare the same weapon's availability and any requirements shown. When a name moves from locked to accessible, you have a direct observed result for your account.

The specific menu label, control key, and slot layout are not documented in the official public description. Do not follow a guide that invents exact button presses without identifying its platform and game version.

sections.heading: Weapon Unlock Requirements and Progress
sections.intro: There is a meaningful distinction between a weapon being listed in the game's description and a requirement that has been independently verified. Use this reference to avoid false unlock tables.

subsections.heading: Which Values Are Confirmed?
paragraphs: The general unlock method is confirmed: kills. Precise totals for Pistol, Shotgun, Sniper, Minigun, Rocket Launcher, and other named items are not published in that description. The simple table below intentionally shows this gap instead of filling it with fabricated figures.

If a future official update introduces a published threshold table, the requirements should be added alongside a version date. A single anecdote without account/version context is insufficient for a universal rule.

subsections.heading: Weapon Names Versus Conditions
paragraphs: The weapons directory records the twelve publicly named tools and handling actions. This tutorial is about how to validate access to them. When you need to check whether an unfamiliar name is even part of the game, use that directory first.

A player may encounter ordinary equipment, locked equipment, and store listings. A label shown by the Roblox storefront is not automatically the same as the kill-based unlock route advertised for gameplay.

sections.heading: What to Do When a Weapon Stays Locked
sections.intro: An unchanged lock after a match does not by itself prove a bug. Check what the current interface actually recorded and make sure you are looking at the same item in the same account.

subsections.heading: Check the Account, Game Version, and Visible Counter
paragraphs: First confirm you rejoined the same game and account. Next, inspect any visible requirement text and compare it with your earlier record. If the screen gives no counter at all, avoid guessing that a certain action counted.

Changes following weekly updates can alter the displayed equipment layout. If a menu or lock icon is missing, compare the new interface with the one you recorded rather than assuming an old tutorial's path remains valid.

subsections.heading: Record Evidence Before Reporting a Problem
paragraphs: A useful report includes the game's title or ID, the exact weapon name, the platform you are using, the date, and a screenshot of the lock or requirement message. If available, include a before-and-after display of progress.

This checklist cannot repair a server-side bug, but it helps separate an uncredited action, a mistaken weapon name, and a version-dependent interface change. Do not upload private account credentials or payment details to troubleshooting forums.

sections.heading: Kills Versus Other Access Methods
sections.intro: A game can display purchases and progression in related menus, but the public description's kills statement should not be stretched into an all-items monetization rule.

subsections.heading: Do Not Assume Every Unlock Is a Purchase
paragraphs: The developer explicitly advertises earning weapons through kills. That is why a player should check in-game progression before assuming a Robux purchase is required. Store items, if any, must be evaluated from their live descriptions.

Individual prices, subscription benefits, VIP advantages, and multipliers are not reliably documented by the public game description supplied for this review. We do not offer a checkout or claim any particular item guarantees faster unlocking.

subsections.heading: When to Check the Game Again
paragraphs: If you return after a major update and discover new weapons or different locks, use the live interface as the immediate source of truth. Save the new names and observed requirements with a date before sharing them with others.
For context on developer updates and the reported next event, see the events page. For category and item names, see the weapons directory.

faq.answer: The official Roblox description says you unlock new weapons with kills. Exact requirements for individual items must be checked in the game.

faq.question: How many kills unlock the Shotgun?
faq.answer: The public description does not publish a verified Shotgun kill total. Check the actual requirement displayed in the version you are playing.

faq.question: Can I farm kills to unlock weapons faster?
faq.answer: Kills drive unlocks, but the official listing does not establish a specific farming method, eligible target list or multiplier. Test only ordinary gameplay and compare any visible progress.

faq.question: Do Horde zombies count toward weapon kills?
faq.answer: That specific counting rule has not been confirmed by the official description. Do not assume it works until you can check the live game's progression indicator.

faq.question: Why is my weapon still locked?
faq.answer: Confirm the correct game and account, check the actual requirement on the current interface, then compare the progress or lock state after play.

faq.question: Can I purchase an unlock instead?
faq.answer: Some Roblox experiences have stores, but this game's public description does not define an alternate purchase route for every weapon. Verify current store details before spending.

title: Ragdoll Reality Zombies: Graveyard & Infection Guide
description: Learn how zombies work in Ragdoll Reality: use the graveyard, understand slow and fast zombie types, and see how infection spreads between dummies.

hero.heading: Ragdoll Reality Zombies and Graveyard Guide
hero.lead: To spawn a zombie, throw a dummy into the graveyard. The developer also confirms that bitten dummies can become infected and turn, creating a separate chain-reaction route to more zombies.

sections.heading: How to Spawn Zombies in Ragdoll Reality
sections.intro: The graveyard and infection mechanics come from the game's official Halloween description. Use this section if your search is about creating a zombie, not calling a full wave with Horde.

subsections.heading: Find the Graveyard Area
paragraphs: The official feature description identifies a graveyard location as the place where conversion occurs. It does not publish a compass direction, coordinate, minimap marker or exact distance to the zone. Search for the marked graveyard in the map version you have loaded rather than relying on an invented 'north corner' direction.

If the environment has changed with an update, the current game's visual landmarks take precedence over an old screenshot. The mechanic is confirmed, but a route or coordinates would require live gameplay evidence.

subsections.heading: Throw a Dummy into the Graveyard
paragraphs: According to the developer, placing a dummy into the graveyard by throwing it causes it to rise as a zombie. The practical sequence is to find a dummy you can handle, move it to the graveyard area, and use the available handling interaction to throw it in.

The public description names Grab as an action, but does not give a universal keyboard or mobile touch control for it. Follow your in-game controls; do not assume a key from another Roblox physics experience will work here.

subsections.heading: Recognize the Transformation
paragraphs: The public description describes zombies as enemies that pursue, pounce, and bite. This is how the undead state differs from an ordinary dummy in the advertised gameplay. It does not establish an exact transformation countdown or a guaranteed on-screen sound effect.
After making a conversion, watch the dummy's behavior and nearby targets. If another dummy changes without entering the graveyard, the official bite-infection mechanic may be responsible.

steps.description: Find the graveyard area in the current map; no official coordinates are published.

steps.heading: Bring and throw a dummy
steps.description: Use your available handling controls to move a dummy into that area.

steps.heading: Watch the zombie behavior
steps.description: Look for the chasing, pouncing or biting behavior described by the developer.

sections.heading: Ragdoll Reality Zombie Types
sections.intro: The official listing names slow, normal, and fast zombie variants. Those labels identify three advertised speed categories, but the developer has not attached measured speed, health, or damage stats to them.

subsections.heading: Slow Zombies
paragraphs: Slow is one of the three types named publicly. Relative labels are helpful for orientation, but 'slow' does not establish a fixed movement value or tell us which exact animation plays first.
Observe relative movement in your current session if you are comparing zombie behavior. Avoid treating one visual encounter as a universal spawn probability.

subsections.heading: Normal Zombies
paragraphs: Normal is the middle label provided by the game description. There is no confirmed public chart defining its speed compared with an ordinary dummy or its health relative to another variant.
When documenting a normal zombie, distinguish direct observation from the advertised label. A target's path through obstacles can make comparisons misleading.

subsections.heading: Fast Zombies
paragraphs: Fast is the third advertised type. A fast zombie is relevant to players because it changes how quickly they may need to react, although actual pursuit values and spawn rates have not been released in the public description.
Do not publish precise studs-per-second claims, special drop rates, or fixed numbers of fast enemies per wave without game evidence.

sections.heading: How Zombie Infection Spreads
sections.intro: A zombie can do more than chase the first target: the developer says bitten dummies become infected and turn. This makes infection a second route to zombie creation after a graveyard conversion.

subsections.heading: What Happens When a Dummy Is Bitten?
paragraphs: The official description names the bite as the infection trigger. In plain terms, an ordinary dummy that is bitten may become another zombie. That is distinct from throwing the same dummy directly into the graveyard.
This explanation establishes the transformation relationship, not its precise timing. There is no published number of seconds between bite and change in the official text.

subsections.heading: How a Chain Can Develop
paragraphs: Consider one dummy converted by the graveyard. That zombie can bite another dummy, which then turns and may infect yet another one. The 'graveyard → first zombie → bite → newly infected zombie' chain follows the advertised feature list without inventing a fixed maximum.

The description does not say every bite succeeds, that all variants have equal infection probability, or that converted targets can later be cured. Those claims need separate evidence before appearing in a guide.

subsections.heading: A Safe Way to Observe the Mechanic
paragraphs: Choose a place where you can clearly see two or more dummies, introduce a graveyard-created zombie, and watch for a bite followed by a change in the second target. Keep your observation distinct from unverified statistics.

An observation sheet could note which target was thrown into the graveyard, which target was bitten, and whether the second target visibly changed. This is a way to verify the feature, not a claim of a guaranteed result.

sections.heading: Graveyard Zombies Versus Horde Mode
sections.intro: These two mechanics have different starting actions. Searching for an individual conversion should lead here, while a player looking for instant wave play should use the Horde guide.

subsections.heading: Individual Conversion Versus Wave Start
paragraphs: Graveyard gameplay begins with a dummy you bring to the area. The Horde feature begins with a dedicated button that calls a wave. Both involve zombies, but the player decision and setup are different.

The official listing does not provide a universal numerical wave count, a graveyard cooldown, or a precise maximum simultaneous zombie number. A comparison is still useful without inventing those figures.

subsections.heading: What to Try Next
paragraphs: Try the graveyard route if you want to watch a specific dummy transform or explore infection. Try Horde if you want the wave-start action described by the developer. For either scenario, check which weapons your account can currently access.

Limited-time event details belong to the events page, not this general mechanic guide. October 24 Zombie Night has ended; that date should not be confused with removal or continuation of the base game's Halloween features.

subsections.heading: What the Official Description Actually Confirms
paragraphs: The public description confirms the graveyard conversion, three speed categories, bite-driven infection, and the Horde button. Those features are separate from third-party accounts of time-limited events and possible rewards.
The current game may change rapidly. If you cannot find the graveyard in a later version, look for developer updates before assuming a specific key combination is broken.

subsections.heading: Where to Verify Future Changes
paragraphs: The most direct public reference is the Roblox experience page. Our event timeline records separately sourced scheduled events and distinguishes them from features already advertised in the game description.

title: Ragdoll Reality Horde Mode: How to Start & Survive
description: Find out how Horde mode starts in Ragdoll Reality, what the Horde button does, and how zombie waves differ from graveyard spawning and infection.

hero.heading: Ragdoll Reality Horde Mode Guide
hero.lead: Use the Horde button to start a zombie wave in Ragdoll Reality. The official game description confirms the button and the wave, but does not publish fixed wave counts, button coordinates, or event rewards.

sections.heading: How to Start Horde Mode in Ragdoll Reality
sections.intro: Unlike the graveyard method, which converts one dummy you move, Horde uses a named control to call a group of zombies. That is the central action a player needs to know.

subsections.heading: Step 1: Find the Horde Button
paragraphs: Open the official experience and look for the control labeled Horde in the current interface. The Roblox description confirms the button exists. Its current color, position, and input method are not included in the public text, so a guide should not give a made-up desktop hotkey or mobile screen coordinate.

If the control is not immediately visible, verify you are in the correct experience and that the live UI still supports the mode. Platform layouts can differ. An older screenshot is less reliable than what your current session shows.

subsections.heading: Step 2: Trigger a Zombie Wave
paragraphs: Activate the Horde control when ready. The game's own description states that pressing it starts a zombie wave. This is what distinguishes a wave-start command from carrying an individual dummy into the graveyard.

No public wave-size, cooldown, minimum kill count, or cost appears in the verified description. If the live game prompts you for another action, use the requirements actually displayed instead of treating an unsourced guide as final.

subsections.heading: Step 3: Watch the Wave and Stay Mobile
paragraphs: After the command, look for the wave of zombies the game advertises. The same description names zombies that chase, pounce, and bite, so staying aware of moving targets is a reasonable player tactic.
The game page does not define how many rounds follow the first wave or how victory is signaled. Do not mistake general survival suggestions for a verified speedrun route or a promise of rewards.

sections.heading: Horde Mode Compared With Regular Zombies
sections.intro: Horde and graveyard spawning belong to the same Halloween set of features but serve different purposes. The comparison below helps you choose the correct action first.

subsections.heading: Graveyard: Convert a Particular Dummy
paragraphs: The graveyard mechanic is hands-on: you take a dummy to the graveyard and it becomes a zombie. That is well suited to observing the transformation or subsequent infection of nearby dummies.

Its main requirement is having a dummy to manipulate and reaching the graveyard. Specific movement controls and map routes are not documented in the official description; the zombies guide focuses on this path.

subsections.heading: Horde: Call a Wave
paragraphs: Horde removes the individual-dummy setup step: the named button starts a wave. The official description does not quantify how many enemies that means or whether waves become progressively larger.
Searchers looking for 'zombie waves' are best served by the Horde page, while 'graveyard location' and 'how to infect dummies' fit the zombie page.

sections.heading: Horde Survival Preparation
sections.intro: The advertised enemies can chase, pounce, and bite. Beyond those behaviors, there are no published official combat formulas for standard Horde mode. Practical preparation can still focus on what you can observe in your own session.

subsections.heading: Check Your Available Weapons
paragraphs: Before starting, look at the equipment you can actually use. The game advertises a large weapon roster and kill-based unlocks, but it does not publish a definitive 'best Horde weapon' list or numeric damage per second.

A player who wants to compare tools can begin with the developer-named equipment list. Choose items familiar to you and avoid buying a gamepass on the unsupported assumption that it is required to participate.

subsections.heading: Read the Space Before You Activate Horde
paragraphs: The game's playground contains environmental hazards including a shredder, train, spike pit and wrecking ball. Those are advertised map features, but no official source says that every Horde arena includes all of them or that a trap guarantees a wave clear.

Check exits, sightlines and nearby obstacles in your current session. Keep moving when enemies approach and observe which interactions are actually available. These are general preparation choices, not a map-specific route verified by a game recording.

subsections.heading: Do Not Confuse Infection With Wave Completion
paragraphs: Bitten dummies can also turn into zombies, according to the official description. That is a separate mechanic from the Horde button's initial wave, so an increase in moving enemies does not by itself prove a new scripted round has started.
Until a wave counter, timer, or victory condition is documented from the game, avoid publishing a fixed round count. Report what the live session shows if you are tracking progress.

sections.heading: How to Verify Changes to Horde Mode
sections.intro: Weekly game updates can alter the interface or event settings. This guide follows the latest confirmed public description and labels the gaps rather than filling them with fictional mechanics.

subsections.heading: What Is Confirmed and What Is Not
paragraphs: Confirmed: there is a Horde button and it starts a zombie wave. Also confirmed elsewhere in the official description: three zombie speed labels and a bite infection mechanic. Not confirmed: fixed enemy totals, wave timers, special boss schedules or baseline rewards.
When you see a claim such as 'wave seven always spawns a boss', ask whether it is dated, from a real gameplay capture, and about regular Horde rather than the October 24 event.

subsections.heading: When Your Button Looks Different
paragraphs: If the actual UI differs from another screenshot, identify the current platform, game title, and date. It is more useful to locate the mode in your live session than to use a supposed keyboard shortcut copied from a similar game.
For the one-dummy graveyard method, follow the zombies page. For equipment names and the kills-based unlock system, use the weapons and unlock guides.

faq.question: How do I start Horde mode in Ragdoll Reality?
faq.answer: The official Roblox description says pressing the Horde button starts a zombie wave. Find that control in the current game UI.

faq.question: Where is the Horde button?
faq.answer: The official public description names the button but does not specify its on-screen location or keyboard key. Check your current game's interface.

faq.question: How many waves are in Horde mode?
faq.answer: An official fixed wave count has not been established from the public game description. Do not confuse ordinary Horde with the October 24 special event.

faq.question: Does Horde have a boss and special rewards?
faq.answer: Those details appear in third-party reporting about a limited Zombie Night event, not as verified permanent rules for standard Horde mode.

faq.question: Can zombies infect other dummies during Horde?
faq.answer: Bite-driven infection exists in Ragdoll Reality, but the public description does not specify detailed interaction rules for each Horde wave.

faq.question: How is Horde different from the graveyard?
faq.answer: Press Horde to create a wave; throw a dummy into the graveyard to convert that individual dummy. The full comparison is in the zombies guide.

sections.heading: Event Times by Region
sections.intro: The calendar expresses the October 28 window in U.S. Eastern time during daylight saving time. On October 28, the correct zone abbreviation is EDT, not EST. Regions may be on different calendar dates even for the same moment.

subsections.heading: October 28 Event: Eastern Time and UTC
paragraphs: 1:00 p.m. EDT equals 17:00 UTC. The reported end time, 6:00 p.m. EDT, equals 22:00 UTC. Always include the date, because a multi-hour window may cross midnight for audiences in Asia and Oceania.
Eastern daylight time uses UTC−4 on October 28. Converting from this offset is safer than copying a page's ambiguous 'your time' label, which may depend on the visitor's device settings.

subsections.heading: Examples for Other Regions
paragraphs: For the reported event window: U.S. Pacific is October 28, 10:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m. PDT; London is October 28, 5:00–10:00 p.m. GMT because U.K. daylight saving time has ended; Tokyo is October 29, 2:00–7:00 a.m. JST.

If a newly updated official schedule changes the original start or end, every converted window should be recomputed. Times in this section are calculations from the third-party reported EDT range, not separately issued regional announcements.

sections.heading: How to Follow Official Ragdoll Reality Updates
sections.intro: Start with the Roblox experience, because the creator may change the listing or publish a newer event there. Use outside calendars to discover a potential event, then treat the game itself as the authority on playable features.

subsections.heading: Official Experience and Event Listings
paragraphs: The official game page has the right experience ID and is where its creator's latest public description appears. Its wording currently promises regular weekly changes. If you see an event on Roblox, use that listing for the most current displayed date and the platform's own notification control if available.
This fan-made guide does not have access to live Roblox account notifications or server update feeds. It should not claim it refreshes every hour or that subscribing here will send you an alert.

subsections.heading: Sources and Corrections
paragraphs: The two kinds of source used on this page are the public Roblox game description and a dated external event schedule. We show the October 26 review date above and mark the event listings by their confidence level rather than calling every reported detail official.

Sources: the official Roblox experience and the published AllThingsHow Ragdoll Reality events schedule. Before relying on a start time or joining for an advertised reward, verify the current Roblox event listing.
